raw_response:
My land is about 4.5 mu here in Quzhou. My son is in Baoding, my daughter in Shijiazhuang — they send money home when they can, but I still farm. I've been doing this since I was a boy. At 74, my knees ache in the cold, so I hire the village machinery cooperative for the plowing and harvest. I do the watching, the watering, the fertilizing myself.

I will grow winter wheat this fall on my 4 mu plot, like I always do. Then right after the wheat comes off in June, I'll put summer maize in on the same ground — no need to plow again, just direct seed into the stubble. The machinery station does that for me now. This wheat-then-maize rotation is what this land does. It's what the land here is good for. I'm not going to try cotton or peanuts at my age, on my own.

I'll keep a half-mu of vegetables by the house — some garlic, beans, cabbage. Mostly for eating, sell a bit at the village market.

For seeds I'll go to the township seed station and get whatever variety they're pushing this year with the subsidy card — probably Jimai 22 or something similar for the wheat, and a hybrid maize like Zhengdan 958 or Xianyu 335. These are reliable. I've used them before.

Fertilizer: I'll put down compound fertilizer as base dressing before seeding, then topdress the wheat with urea at jointing. For maize I'll do the same — compound at planting, urea at jointing. I know the agronomist from the county says I use too much nitrogen. Maybe. But I've seen what happens when wheat goes thin. I'll use what I've always used.

Wheat needs three waterings here — one before winter sets in, one at jointing, one at heading. Maize just needs one if the summer rains are short. I'll watch the sky.

Two pesticide applications for the wheat — one for powdery mildew around April, one for aphids before harvest. One for the maize if I see corn borer or blight. I don't spray more than I need to; the chemicals cost money.
